formal_statement: If absorption rewrites a source witness without changing payload/status semantics, counterexample status is preserved.
conclusion: source and absorbed witness have the same counterexample status
reason: Preservation alone is too strong because the intended branch may be contradiction/refutation rather than witness preservation.

formal_statement: If the absorption target is the same obstruction payload covered by the bounded family-chain theorem, the target counterexample status is refuted.
assumptions: valid target;bounded theorem applies;source-target payload/status alignment
conclusion: target status is refuted by contradiction
reason: This is usable as a branch, but source refutation still needs alignment between lifted target and source counterexample.

formal_statement: If direct refutation is unavailable and absorption produces a normalized residual witness with strict lexicographic decrease, status is reduced to a smaller witness.
reason: Residual measure decrease remains open, so this cannot be promoted as completed.

formal_statement: For a recognized absorption trigger, family-chain absorption either refutes the matching target/source status, reduces to a strictly smaller witness under residual measure decrease, or routes failure to a named blocker or higher-support escape.
assumptions: absorption notation/semantics;fresh target package;status language;escape interface
reason: Selected because it keeps contradiction, smaller-witness, and failure branches distinct without proving arbitrary absorption congruence.

formal_statement: Every support-growth witness satisfying any family-chain absorption language has full preservation/refutation/reduction congruence.
reason: Out of scope; lower-layer 7/7 freshness and limited theorem applicability do not imply arbitrary absorption status proof.
